title: Multiparametric analyses of tumor cell and microenvironmental factors to identify biomarkers of therapy response and disease course in patients with head and neck tumors
summary: This study focuses on head and neck squamous cell carcinomas, a diverse group of tumors that often have a poor prognosis. A new approach— administering immune checkpoint therapy several weeks before surgery—is becoming standard for patients with tumors that can be removed, but not everyone benefits equally. Our goal is to understand why some tumors stop responding to this treatment and how the body’s own immune cells enter and act within the tumor environment. By uncovering these insights, we aim to identify markers that predict who will respond well to immune therapy and who will not. We will also explore novel immune-modulating and immune-cell-based treatments and investigate how best to combine them with surgery, radiation, or chemotherapy to improve patients’ outcomes and quality of life.
conditions: Malignant neoplasms of lip, oral cavity and pharynx
Malignant neoplasm of other and ill-defined sites

interventions.name: Patients with head and neck tumors who received perioperative and/or neoadjuvant immune checkpoint therapy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Treatment of a head and neck tumor with neoadjuvant/perioperative immune checkpoint therapy
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of consent
- Pregnant and breastfeeding patients
- Non-German-speaking individuals if there is no possibility of barrier-free communication in English or if a certified translation is unavailable during the informed consent discussion
- Individuals who are chronically incapable of understanding information and providing informed consent
